claims.text: The baseline is a conventionally processed FeNiCrCoCu coating on a metal substrate with a uniform elemental distribution and no targeted Cu enrichment.
Processing or deposition conditions can be modified to increase the surface Cu content relative to the baseline coating.
Increasing the Cu-rich character of the coating surface promotes formation of a Cu-rich oxide tribolayer during high-temperature sliding.
The resulting Cu-rich oxide tribolayer is continuous and nanoscale.
Locally increased Cu causes faster oxidation at high temperature.
Locally increased Cu causes more spatially uniform oxidation at high temperature.
The Cu-enhanced surface forms a stable oxide tribolayer during high-temperature sliding.
The oxide tribolayer diminishes direct metal-to-metal asperity contact.
Reduced direct asperity contact lessens severe local plastic deformation.
Reduced direct asperity contact and deformation lower coating wear.
Relative to the baseline, the Cu-enhanced coating will have a lower wear rate under oxidation-permitting high-temperature sliding.
Relative to the baseline, the Cu-enhanced coating will exhibit milder microscopic deformation, including reduced microcracking or shear localization.
The predicted mechanism is expected to operate during sliding at approximately 500–700 °C under controlled load and an atmosphere that permits oxidation.
The mechanism requires oxidation kinetics sufficiently rapid to form the tribolayer.
At lower temperatures, the tribolayer may not form effectively.
At lower temperatures, Cu surface enrichment may have negligible effects on wear and microscopic deformation.
Prior studies suggest that oxide tribolayers can improve wear resistance.
The magnitude of wear improvement and the tribolayer's thickness and continuity depend on environmental, loading, and compositional factors.
